mainTopic: רבי's permission of בית שאן and the challenges to it, the respect owed to a תלמיד חכם's new הלכה, and the story of רבי פנחס בן יאיר and his animal.
overview: This amud finishes רבי's answer to his family about permitting the produce of בית שאן. Just as earlier kings left חזקיהו room to make his mark, רבי's ancestors left him room to make his. From this the גמרא learns that a תלמיד חכם who says a new הלכה must not be pushed aside. It gives three wordings of this lesson, each with its own source. Then יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי asks how בית שאן could be outside ארץ ישראל. The answer is that עולי בבל never conquered it, and רבי holds that the first holiness of the land was only for its time. Next, רבי ירמיה raises several doubts about the proof from רבי מאיר eating a leaf there without tithing, and רבי זירא answers each one. The phrase 'animals of the righteous' leads to the story of רבי פנחס בן יאיר, for whom the river גינאי split. The amud ends as his donkey refuses barley at an inn, and the story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: My ancestors left me room to make my mark
steps.stepSummary: רבי ends his answer: just as חזקיהו's ancestors left him something to fix, his own ancestors left him room to make his mark by permitting בית שאן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, his ancestors left him room to make his mark. I too: my ancestors left me room to make my mark.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי finishes his answer to his family, who asked how he could permit what his ancestors had treated as forbidden. He compares himself to חזקיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Great kings before חזקיהו did not destroy the נחש הנחושת, yet that does not mean they wanted it to stay. They simply left it for him to do. In the same way, the fact that רבי's ancestors never permitted בית שאן does not prove it is forbidden. They left that ruling for him.

keyTerms.meaning: They left him room, an open space for him to do something
To make one's mark or gain distinction through it

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea: a later scholar may decide something new even if earlier great people never ruled that way.

phrases.english: Rather, his ancestors left him a place
phrases.notes: "His" means חזקיהו, who destroyed the copper snake that earlier kings had left standing.

phrases.english: through which to make his mark;

phrases.aramaic: אַף אֲנִי מָקוֹם הִנִּיחוּ לִי אֲבוֹתַי
phrases.english: I too, my ancestors left me a place
through which to make my mark.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מָקוֹם הִנִּיחוּ לוֹ אֲבוֹתָיו לְהִתְגַּדֵּר בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי's reply, which began before this section, to his family's objection about permitting בית שאן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Analogy to a precedent (חזקיהו and the נחש הנחושת)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If earlier great generations did not permit בית שאן, it must be forbidden, and a later scholar cannot permit it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Earlier generations may leave a matter open on purpose. A later scholar can rightly be the one to rule on it.

steps.title: Do not push aside a scholar who says a new הלכה
steps.stepSummary: From רבי's story we learn that a תלמיד חכם who says a new הלכה must not be dismissed. The lesson comes in three versions.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here we learn about a Torah scholar who says a matter of הלכה: we do not move him. Some say: we do not reject him. Some say: we do not call him arrogant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a general lesson from רבי's words and gives three versions of how it was worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three versions differ by one word: מזיחין (moving him from his position), מזניחין (rejecting or ignoring him), and מזחיחין (calling his new idea arrogance). All three agree that a new הלכה from a scholar deserves respect.

keyTerms.meaning: A ruling of Jewish law, here a new one
Moving or pushing someone out of place

steps.confusionAlert: These are not three separate rules. They are three wordings of one lesson, and each has a slightly different meaning.

phrases.english: From here, regarding a Torah scholar
who said a matter of הלכה,
that we do not move him;
and some say: we do not reject him;
and some say: we do not call him arrogant.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁאָמַר דְּבַר הֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general lesson from רבי's statement in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם who says a new הלכה must not be pushed aside, ignored, or called arrogant.

steps.title: Where each of the three words comes from
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a source for each of the three words: a פסוק about the חושן, a פסוק from איכה, and a teaching about arrogant hearts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says מזיחין: as it says, "the breastplate shall not move." The one who says מזניחין: as it says, "For ה׳ will not abandon forever." The one who says מזחיחין: as we learned, "Once the arrogant-hearted grew many, arguments grew many in Israel."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the meaning of each of the three versions by pointing to where the word appears elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יזח with the חושן means moving out of place, so מזיחין means removing the scholar from his position. יזנח means abandoning, so מזניחין means ignoring him. זחוחי הלב means arrogant people, so מזחיחין means saying his new ruling comes from pride.

keyTerms.meaning: The breastplate worn by the כהן גדול
Will move or slip out of place

steps.whatToRemember: Each wording matches a source: יזח means move, יזנח means abandon, and זחוחי הלב means arrogant. All three teach respect for a scholar's new ruling.

phrases.english: The one who says "move" —
as it is written: "And the breastplate shall not move";
and the one who says "we do not reject" —
as it is written: "For ה׳ will not abandon forever";
and the one who says "call arrogant" —
as we learned: once the arrogant-hearted increased,
disputes increased in Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר מְזִיחִין כְּדִכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the three versions listed in step 2 by giving a source for each word.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each version's word is explained by a parallel use: moving (חושן), abandoning (איכה), and arrogance (זחוחי הלב).

steps.title: Isn't בית שאן part of ארץ ישראל?
steps.stepSummary: יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי asks how anyone could say בית שאן is outside ארץ ישראל, when a פסוק lists it as land of שבט מנשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי challenged: Does anyone really say בית שאן is not part of ארץ ישראל? Doesn't it say: "And מנשה did not drive out בית שאן and its villages, and תענך and its villages"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main issue and challenges the basic idea behind רבי's ruling: that בית שאן is not treated as ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says שבט מנשה failed to drive out the people of בית שאן. That shows בית שאן was part of מנשה's share of the land, inside ארץ ישראל. So how could its produce be exempt from מעשרות? Steps 5 and 6 answer this.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it, raised a strong objection based on reasoning or a source
The Land of Israel, where the land-based מצוות apply
Did not drive out, did not conquer
Literally "its daughters": the small towns around a city

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether בית שאן was fully conquered. The פסוק admits it was not. The point is that being listed in מנשה's share shows it belongs to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי:
phrases.english: Yehuda, son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, challenged it:
And is there anyone who says

phrases.aramaic: דְּבֵית שְׁאָן לָאו מֵאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הִיא?
phrases.english: that בית שאן is not part of ארץ ישראל?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכְתִיב: ״וְלֹא הוֹרִישׁ מְנַשֶּׁה אֶת בֵּית שְׁאָן וְאֶת בְּנוֹתֶיהָ
phrases.english: But isn't it written: "And מנשה did not drive out בית שאן and its villages,
and תענך and its villages"!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side lesson about scholars and goes back to challenge the basic ruling that בית שאן is exempt.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea behind רבי's ruling that בית שאן is not treated as ארץ ישראל for מעשרות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק lists בית שאן as land שבט מנשה was supposed to conquer, which places it inside ארץ ישראל. So its produce should need מעשרות.

steps.title: He forgot that the returnees from Babylonia did not conquer every city
steps.stepSummary: The questioner forgot a teaching: many cities conquered by those who left מצרים were not conquered again by those who came back from בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The questioner did not know this teaching of רבי שמעון בן אליקים, in the name of רבי אלעזר בן פדת, in the name of רבי אלעזר בן שמוע: Many cities were conquered by those who came up from מצרים, but were not conquered by those who came up from בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 4. Yes, בית שאן was part of יהושע's conquest, but it was not part of the later conquest by the people who returned from בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that a פסוק counting בית שאן as land of שבט מנשה settles the matter for all time. The answer shows there were two separate conquests. A city could be in the first conquest and still be missing from the second.

keyTerms.meaning: It escaped him; he did not know or forgot this teaching
Those who came up from מצרים, the generation of יהושע who first conquered the land
Those who came up from בבל, the returnees in the time of עזרא

phrases.english: This escaped his attention:
phrases.notes: "His" means the one who asked the question in step 4, יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי.

phrases.english: what Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim said
in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן שַׁמּוּעַ:
phrases.english: who said it in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua:
Many cities were conquered by those who came up from Egypt,
but were not conquered by those who came up from Babylonia.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִישְׁתְּמִיטְתֵּיהּ הָא דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Missing information: the questioner did not know about two separate conquests
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A פסוק listing בית שאן as land of מנשה would mean it is holy ארץ ישראל forever
steps.terutzMaskana: בית שאן was conquered by עולי מצרים but not by עולי בבל

steps.title: The first holiness of the land was only for its time
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds that the holiness from יהושע's conquest ended. The returnees from בבל left some places unconsecrated so poor people could rely on them during שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי holds: The first holiness made the land holy only for its own time, not for the future. The returnees left those places out so that poor people could rely on them during the שביעית year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer by explaining why it matters that עולי בבל did not conquer בית שאן. According to רבי, only the second holiness still counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 alone is not enough, because one could say יהושע's conquest still makes the land holy. Here we learn that רבי holds the first holiness ended with the exile. Places that עולי בבל left out on purpose, so the poor could farm and eat there in שביעית, have no obligation of land-based מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds; this is his view
The first holiness of ארץ ישראל, from יהושע's conquest
The seventh year, when the land may not be farmed

steps.whyThisMatters: Whether the first holiness lasts forever is a major question that decides which areas of ארץ ישראל are obligated in תרומות, מעשרות and שביעית.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying בית שאן is not part of ארץ ישראל at all. It is saying that, by רבי's view, the land-based מצוות do not apply there after the exile.

phrases.english: And he holds: The first holiness
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי, who permitted בית שאן.

phrases.english: made the land holy for its time
but did not make it holy for the future,
and they left them out so that they could rely on them,
phrases.notes: "They" are the returnees from בבל, and "them" are the cities they did not consecrate.

phrases.english: the poor, during the Sabbatical Year.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 5 by giving רבי's underlying view
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the legal principle that makes step 5 relevant
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי, only the holiness of עולי בבל counts, so בית שאן is exempt
steps.whatToRemember: בית שאן was conquered by יהושע but not by עזרא's returnees. רבי holds the first holiness ended, so בית שאן is exempt from land-based מצוות.

steps.title: רבי מאיר only ate a single leaf
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks: how can we prove anything from רבי מאיר, when all he ate was a leaf, which may be eaten as a snack without tithing?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זירא: But רבי מאיר only ate a leaf!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge begins. רבי ירמיה questions the proof that רבי relied on, the testimony that רבי מאיר ate a leaf in בית שאן without tithing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even in a place that must tithe, a person may eat a small casual snack before tithing. So eating one leaf without tithing would not prove that רבי מאיר held בית שאן is exempt.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Zeira:
But Rabbi Meir,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the earlier testimony that רבי מאיר ate a vegetable leaf in בית שאן without tithing.

phrases.english: it was merely a leaf that he ate!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר עָלֶה בְּעָלְמָא הוּא דְּאָכֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the reason for רבי's ruling to the evidence he relied on
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from רבי מאיר eating a leaf in בית שאן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A casual snack may be eaten before tithing anywhere, so the act proves nothing about בית שאן being exempt

steps.title: The leaf came from a bundle
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that the leaf came from a tied bundle, and a bundled vegetable already needs tithing even for a snack.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He ate it from a bundle, and we learned in a משנה: A vegetable that is tied in bundles needs tithing from the moment it is tied.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא defends the proof. The leaf came from a finished bundle, so even a snack from it would need tithing in a place that is obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce becomes fully obligated in tithes once its processing is complete, and for bundled vegetables that happens when they are tied. After that point, even casual eating is forbidden before tithing. So רבי מאיר's eating does show he held בית שאן is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: A vegetable that is usually tied in bundles
From when it is tied; the point it becomes obligated in tithes

phrases.english: He said to him: He ate it from a bundle,
and we learned: A vegetable that is bundled, from when it is bundled.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in מעשרות 1:5. From that moment it owes tithes, so even a snack is forbidden before tithing.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵאֲגוּדָּה אַכְלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the facts of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It was a casual snack that is allowed without tithing
steps.terutzMaskana: It came from a bundle, which needs tithing even for a snack

steps.title: Maybe he was not paying attention
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks: perhaps רבי מאיר ate the leaf without thinking, so his act proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it was not on his mind?
steps.whatsHappening: A second challenge to the proof. Maybe רבי מאיר simply did not notice what he was doing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 showed the leaf needed tithing. Now the doubt moves from the law to רבי מאיר himself: an absent-minded act cannot teach us a הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Not on his mind; he was not paying attention

phrases.english: But perhaps it was not on his mind?
phrases.notes: רבי ירמיה is still the one asking, and "his" means רבי מאיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא לָאו אַדַּעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge after step 8 answered the first one
steps.kashyaTarget: The reliability of רבי מאיר's act as a proof
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he ate without paying attention, the act does not show his halachic view

steps.title: ה׳ does not let the righteous stumble
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers with a קל וחומר‎: ה׳ does not let even the animals of צדיקים cause a mishap, so surely He protects the צדיקים themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, if ה׳ does not bring about a mishap even through the animals of the righteous, then surely not through the righteous themselves!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא rejects the idea that רבי מאיר ate by mistake. A צדיק like him would be protected from such an error.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer uses a קל וחומר: if ה׳ guards even the animals of צדיקים from causing a sin, He certainly guards the צדיקים themselves. So רבי מאיר's act was on purpose, and it proves he held בית שאן is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Now; introduces a "how much more so" argument

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from רבי מאיר holds: the leaf needed tithing, and a צדיק like him would not eat it by mistake.

phrases.english: Now, the animals of the righteous,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not
bring about a mishap through them,
the righteous themselves, all the more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא, בְּהֶמְתָּן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מֵבִיא תַּקָּלָה עַל יָדָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: קל וחומר from divine protection of the righteous
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר may have eaten without thinking
steps.terutzMaskana: A צדיק would not stumble like that, so his act was deliberate and is a valid proof

steps.title: Maybe he tithed from somewhere else
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה suggests that רבי מאיר tithed the leaves by separating from other produce in a different place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps רבי מאיר tithed those leaves using produce from another place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה raises a new doubt. Maybe רבי מאיר did tithe the leaf, just by taking the tithe from produce somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי מאיר tithed in a way nobody saw, his eating proves nothing about בית שאן being exempt. The proof that רבי exempted בית שאן would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: From another place, meaning from produce located elsewhere

phrases.english: And perhaps he tithed for them from another place?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא עִישֵּׂר עֲלֵיהֶם מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the answer that צדיקים don't stumble, רבי ירמיה raises a different possible explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from רבי מאיר's eating that בית שאן was exempt from tithes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The act can be explained as tithing done elsewhere, so it does not show an exemption.

steps.title: A חבר only tithes from nearby produce
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that careful people (חברים) never separate תרומה from produce that is not close by.
steps.simpleTranslation: חברים are not suspected of separating תרומה from produce that is not right next to it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא rejects the idea. Someone careful like רבי מאיר would not tithe from produce that is far away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proper way is to tithe from produce that is right next to the produce being fixed. A חבר always does it the proper way, so רבי מאיר did not tithe from another place.

keyTerms.meaning: People who are trusted to be careful with tithes and purity
They are not suspected (of doing something improper)
Produce that is close by, right next to the produce being tithed

phrases.english: חברים are not suspected
to separate תרומה from what is not nearby.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נֶחְשְׁדוּ חֲבֵרִים לִתְרוֹם שֶׁלֹּא מִן הַמּוּקָּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A general rule about how careful people behave rules out the suggestion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר might have tithed the leaf from produce in another place.
steps.terutzMaskana: A חבר like רבי מאיר tithes only from nearby produce, so that did not happen.

steps.title: Maybe he set aside tithes in his mind
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה suggests that רבי מאיר mentally set aside one side of the vegetable as tithes and ate from the other side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he set his eyes on this side of the vegetable as the tithe and ate from the other side.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה tries one more doubt. Maybe רבי מאיר chose part of the same vegetable as the tithe in his mind, and then ate from the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers Step 12's point, because the tithe would be from the same produce and therefore nearby. If so, the act again proves nothing about an exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: He set his eyes, meaning he mentally designated

phrases.english: And perhaps he set his eyes on this side
phrases.notes: He means he decided in his mind that this side of the vegetable would be the tithe.

phrases.english: and ate from the other side?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא נָתַן עֵינָיו בְּצַד זֶה וְאָכַל בְּצַד אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gets around Step 12's answer by suggesting a tithe taken from the same nearby produce.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from רבי מאיר's eating
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A silent mental designation would allow eating without any exemption, so the act proves nothing.

steps.title: Trust the great witness
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that the person who reported the story is a great man, so his report is accurate.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Look at how great the man is who is testifying about him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers by pointing to the witness. A man that great reported exactly what רבי מאיר did, so we can trust the report.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witness (רבי יהושע בן זרוז) was a great man who carefully reported that רבי מאיר ate without tithing. We do not invent hidden actions he would have noticed and told us about.
steps.whatToRemember: In the end, every attempt to explain away רבי מאיר's eating is rejected. The proof stands that בית שאן was treated as exempt from tithes.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזִי מַאן גַּבְרָא רַבָּה
phrases.english: He said to him: See who the great man is
phrases.notes: רבי זירא is answering רבי ירמיה.

phrases.english: who is testifying about him.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲזִי מַאן גַּבְרָא רַבָּה קָמַסְהֵיד עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 13 and closes the challenges to the proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relies on how reliable the witness is.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר may have tithed in his mind, without anyone knowing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The great witness's report is precise, so רבי מאיר really ate without tithing.

steps.title: What are the 'animals of the righteous'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what story the phrase 'animals of the righteous' refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the story behind 'the animals of the righteous'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the phrase from Step 10 and asks where it comes from. This sets up a story that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said that ה׳ does not let even the animals of צדיקים cause a mishap. Now the גמרא wants to know which event that idea is based on.

phrases.english: What is 'the animals of the righteous'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בְּהֶמְתָּן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the tithing discussion and explains a phrase used in Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which event shows that ה׳ protects even the animals of צדיקים.

steps.title: רבי פנחס בן יאיר reaches the river
steps.stepSummary: The story begins: רבי פנחס בן יאיר was traveling to redeem captives and came to the river גינאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי פנחס בן יאיר was going to redeem captives, and he came to the river גינאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins the story that answers the question. רבי פנחס בן יאיר is on his way to do a מצוה, and a river blocks his path.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story opens by showing that he was busy with the great מצוה of freeing captives. That fact will matter in his argument with the river.

keyTerms.meaning: Redeeming captives, buying the freedom of people being held prisoner

phrases.english: That רבי פנחס בן יאיר
was going to redeem captives,
he came upon the river גינאי.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר הֲוָה קָאָזֵיל לְפִדְיוֹן שְׁבוּיִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase comes from the story of רבי פנחס בן יאיר. The story continues in the next steps.

steps.title: He asks the river to split
steps.stepSummary: רבי פנחס בן יאיר tells the river to split its water so he can cross.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to it: גינאי, split your water for me and I will pass through you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי פנחס בן יאיר speaks to the river and asks it to split so he can pass.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צדיק speaks directly to nature and expects it to make way for his מצוה. This leads to the river's answer in the next step.

phrases.english: He said to it: גינאי,
split your water for me and I will pass through you!

steps.triggerLanguage: גִּינַּאי, חֲלוֹק לִי מֵימֶךָ וְאֶעֱבוֹר בָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The צדיק commands the river to make way for him.

steps.title: The river refuses
steps.stepSummary: The river argues that it is also doing ה׳'s will, and its success is certain while his is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It said to him: You are going to do your Maker's will, and I am going to do my Maker's will. You may or may not succeed, but I will certainly succeed.
steps.whatsHappening: The river pushes back with an argument. Both of them are serving ה׳, and the river's job is the surer one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The river's job is to flow, and it will surely do that. His mission might fail, for example if he cannot free the captives. So why should the certain job give way to the uncertain one?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַתָּה הוֹלֵךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹן קוֹנֶךָ
phrases.english: It said to him: You are going to do the will of your Maker
and I am going to do the will of my Maker,
you may succeed in doing it
or you may not succeed in doing it,
I will certainly do it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה הוֹלֵךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹן קוֹנֶךָ וַאֲנִי הוֹלֵךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹן קוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The river argues against the request of Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי פנחס בן יאיר's demand that the river split
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A certain fulfillment of ה׳'s will should not give way to one that is only possible.

steps.title: The decree, and the river splits
steps.stepSummary: רבי פנחס בן יאיר warns that if the river does not split, he will decree that it dries up forever, and the river splits.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to it: If you do not split, I decree on you that water will never flow through you. It split for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי פנחס בן יאיר answers the river with a decree that it will dry up forever. The river gives in and splits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not argue back point by point. He shows that he can take away the river's own job completely. The river splitting shows how much power a צדיק has.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִם אִי אַתָּה חוֹלֵק
phrases.english: He said to it: If you do not split,
I decree upon you
that water will never pass through you.
It split for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אִי אַתָּה חוֹלֵק גּוֹזְרַנִי עָלֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overcomes the river's refusal in Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A threat that would make the river unable to do its job at all.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The river's certain mission should win out.
steps.terutzMaskana: The צדיק's decree wins, and the river splits.

steps.title: Splitting for the man with wheat for פסח
steps.stepSummary: A man carrying wheat for פסח was there, and רבי פנחס בן יאיר had the river split for him too, because he was busy with a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man carrying wheat for פסח. He said to the river: Split for this man too, since he is busy with a מצוה. It split for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. A second traveler, who was carrying wheat for מצה, also gets to cross.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason given is that this man was also busy with a מצוה. That matches the idea that ה׳ helps people who are on their way to do a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: He is busy with a מצוה

phrases.english: There was a certain man
who was carrying wheat for פסח,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ חֲלוֹק לֵיהּ נָמֵי לְהַאי,
phrases.english: he said to it: Split for this one too,
phrases.notes: רבי פנחס בן יאיר is talking to the river again.

phrases.english: since he is busy with a מצוה.
It split for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דַּהֲוָה דָּארֵי חִיטֵּי לְפִיסְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story with a second traveler.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The river splits for someone busy with a מצוה.

steps.title: Splitting for the traveler who joined them
steps.stepSummary: A non-Jewish traveler was walking with them, and the river split for him too, so he would not complain that his companions abandoned him.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an Arab traveling with them. He said to the river: Split for this one too, so he will not say, 'This is how people treat a traveling companion?' It split for him.
steps.whatsHappening: A third traveler, a non-Jew who was walking with them, also gets to cross. The reason is so he will not feel abandoned by the people he was traveling with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This man was not doing a מצוה. He was helped out of fairness and good manners toward a travel companion, to avoid a bad impression. The story continues on the next lines with the 'animals' part.

keyTerms.meaning: Traveling companions, people who walk along with you

phrases.english: There was a certain Arab
who was traveling along with them,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ חֲלוֹק לֵיהּ נָמֵי לְהַאי,
phrases.english: he said to it: Split for this one too,
so that he should not say:
'This is what one does to traveling companions?!'
It split for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה הָהוּא טַיָּיעָא דִּלְוָוה בַּהֲדַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story with a third traveler, who was helped for a different reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The river splits even for a non-Jewish companion, so that he will not feel mistreated.

steps.title: Greater than משה and all of Israel
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says רבי פנחס בן יאיר was greater than משה and the six hundred thousand, since ים סוף split once but the river split three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: How great is this man, greater than משה and the six hundred thousand! There the water split one time, and here it split three times.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף looks back at the river story and praises רבי פנחס בן יאיר, saying he was even greater than משה and the whole nation at ים סוף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His proof is a simple count. At ים סוף the water split once, but the river split three times: once for רבי פנחס בן יאיר, once for the man carrying wheat, and once for the traveler.

keyTerms.meaning: sixty times ten thousand, meaning the six hundred thousand Jews who left מצרים

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
How great is this man,
more than Moshe and the six hundred thousand,
for there it was one time,
phrases.notes: "There" means at ים סוף, when the sea split for the Jews leaving מצרים.

phrases.english: and here three times.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: כַּמָּה נְפִישׁ גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a lesson from the three splittings described in steps 19-21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי פנחס בן יאיר is greater than משה and ישראל, because he had three splittings against their one.

steps.title: Maybe it split only once
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the count: maybe the river split one time and all three crossed together.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps here too it split only one time?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב יוסף's proof by suggesting that the river may have split just once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the river stayed open until all three people had crossed, then there was only one splitting, exactly like ים סוף. That would knock out the reason for calling him 'greater'.

phrases.english: And perhaps here too it was one time?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא הָכָא נָמֵי חֲדָא זִימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof behind רב יוסף's statement in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the river split three separate times
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The story can be read as one long splitting, which would make it equal to ים סוף and not greater.

steps.title: Equal to משה and all of Israel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the praise: he was as great as משה and the six hundred thousand.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he was like משה and the six hundred thousand.
steps.whatsHappening: Because of the challenge, the גמרא lowers רב יוסף's claim from 'greater than' to 'equal to' משה and ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we cannot be sure the river split three times, we can only be sure of one splitting. That matches ים סוף, so the safe conclusion is that he was equal to them.

keyTerms.meaning: like משה, on the same level

steps.whatToRemember: Final version: רבי פנחס בן יאיר was as great as משה and the six hundred thousand, because a body of water split for him just as ים סוף split for them.

phrases.english: Rather, like Moshe and the six hundred thousand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כְּמֹשֶׁה וְשִׁתִּין רִבְּוָון
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 23 and changes the claim of step 22.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי פנחס בן יאיר was equal to משה and ישראל, not greater than them.

steps.title: The donkey refuses the barley at the inn
steps.stepSummary: רבי פנחס בן יאיר comes to an inn. They put barley in front of his donkey, and it does not eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came to a certain inn. They put barley in front of his donkey, and it did not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves to a new scene: at an inn, his donkey refuses its food. This sets up the next part of the story, which will explain why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is explained yet. The גמרא simply reports that the donkey would not eat, and the reason comes in the next lines.

phrases.english: He happened to come to a certain inn,
they put barley before his donkey,
it did not eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִקְּלַע לְהָהוּא אוּשְׁפִּיזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the travels of רבי פנחס בן יאיר after he crosses the river. This is the part of the story about his animal that answers the question of step 15, 'מאי בהמתן של צדיקים'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: His donkey would not eat the barley it was given at the inn.
